what_its_for: Prucalopride is used to treat chronic idiopathic constipation (long-term constipation with no known cause) in adults. It helps your bowels move more regularly by stimulating the muscles in your digestive tract to work better.
how_to_take: Take prucalopride by mouth with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food, at any time of day. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush or chew it.
dosing: The usual dose for most adults is 2 mg once daily. If you are 65 years of age or older, or if you have severe kidney problems, your doctor may start you on a lower dose of 1 mg once daily. Always follow your doctor's instructions about how much to take.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on that same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time. Do not take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store prucalopride at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it in a dry place away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking excessive amounts of alcohol while taking this medicine, as it may worsen side effects like dizziness. Be careful driving or operating machinery until you know how prucalopride affects you, since it may cause dizziness or headaches, especially when you first start taking it.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: severe or ongoing diarrhea, severe stomach pain or cramping, signs of depression or mood changes, thoughts of self-harm or suicide, a fast or irregular heartbeat, swelling of the hands or feet, or if your constipation does not improve after 4 weeks of treatment. Also tell your doctor about all other medications you take before starting prucalopride.
when_it_works: Some people notice improvement within the first few days of taking prucalopride. For others, it may take up to 4 weeks to see the full benefit. If you do not have at least 3 complete, spontaneous bowel movements per week after 4 weeks, talk to your doctor about whether this medicine is right for you.
special_populations: Older adults (age 65 and over): Start with 1 mg once daily. Kidney problems: If you have severe kidney disease, your dose will be lowered to 1 mg once daily. Liver problems: If you have severe liver disease, talk to your doctor, as a dose adjustment may be needed. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before taking this medicine, as its safety in these situations has not been fully established. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children under 18 years of age.
